name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the father of the city of Gibeon. His role as a progenitor of this significant city marks his unique contribution to the biblical record. Scripture does not provide additional details or notes about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means "G-d [El] has preserved," reflecting a theological affirmation of divine preservation. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:35 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant meaning within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Jeiel is connected through inferred family relationships to several individuals including Maacah, identified as his wife, and a list of sons such as Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher, and Mikloth, all noted within 1 Chronicles 8. These relationships indicate Jeiel's role as a patriarch within his family line in the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance in Scripture centers on his foundational role as the father of Gibeon, a city of importance in Israel's history. His mention in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles underscores the continuity of God's covenant people through established family lines and cities. The preservation implied in his name aligns with God's faithfulness in sustaining His chosen people and their heritage.
